title: Barnaby Retail — tactical outreach journal
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for Barnaby Retail outbound — consolidation of account signals, hypothesis for value prop, short email/call drafts, objection handling, and next steps. Not polished. Notes to self.

Account at-a-glance
- Company: Barnaby Retail (mid-market omnichannel retailer; 2.4B annual revenue; ~1.6k stores + web/app)
- HQ: Minneapolis
- Recent signals: raised debt facility (Q3 2025), announced AI merchandising pilot in press release (Oct 2025), LinkedIn hiring: 'Senior ML infra engineer' and 'Head of Digital Ops' roles posted last month.
- Likely org: CTO>Head of Data/ML>ML Platform>Retail Ops/Product for merchandising. Procurement usually via IT/Infrastructure for vendor/contracting.
- Key tech: on-prem data warehouse (Snowflake hybrid), K8s for services, in-house model training, but previous cloud vendor lift described in earnings call.

Pain hypotheses (quick)
- Speed-to-production for LLM features: ML team is focused on training/modeling, not inference ops; ops slows rollouts.
- Cost volatility when scaling inference on cloud GPUs — finance complaining in Q2? (signal: debt facility + margin pressure)
- Compliance/sensitive PII for customer support and returns workflows -> need for private deployment or strict controls.
- Merchandising decisions need low-latency, high-throughput scoring for catalogs and checkout personalization.

Why Redwood might land (angle & hypothesis)
- Pitch: move from prototype to predictable inference economics + SRE-grade SLA. Offer Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput (merch scoring) + Private control plane for PII-sensitive use cases.
- Ops lift reduction: Redwood handles runtime, autoscaling, caching (prefix/KV) — frees ML infra to own models and features.
- Cost story: show TCO vs self-hosted cloud GPU + ops. Prepare 6–12 month comparison: forecast cost per 1M predictions.

Quick ROI callouts to test in outreach (numbers are placeholders)
- If Barnaby currently spends $18k/month on GPU spot for a pilot, Redwood Dedicated could reduce unit cost by ~25% while cutting ops FTE time (0.2–0.5 FTE saved) -> finance-friendly.
- For merchandising scoring at peak, latencies under 50ms for online personalization increase conversion by X (need to confirm with them). Tie to conversion delta -> revenue impact estimates.

Primary decision-makers to target (sequencing)
1) Head of ML/ML Platform (technical decision) — initial POC ask
2) Director of Digital/Product (value/metrics owner) — cares about conversion and UX
3) CTO / VP Infra (procurement & security) — approves Dedicated/Private and contracts
4) Procurement with legal for SOW terms

Outbound email draft (short cold)
Subject: Small POC to speed up Barnaby’s merchandising scoring
Hi <first>,

Quick note — I work with teams like Barnaby’s ML platform to move models from experiments into production predictablely (lower latency, lower token cost, predictable monthly spend). We recently ran a dedicated pilot for a retailer that cut inference unit costs ~25% and eliminated a 0.5 FTE ops backlog.

Would you be open to a 20–30 minute call to see a short POC plan for merchandising scoring (we handle runtime, autoscaling, and private deployment options)?

If yes — I’ll send 2 time slots and a 1-page POC sketch.

Best,
Aisha

Call script bullets (20–30m intro / discovery)
- Intro: quick, 90s. Name, Redwood, very short one-liner.
- Confirm context: noticed merchandising AI pilot; ask where the blocking points are (ops, cost, latency, compliance?)
- Explore traffic patterns: qps, peak windows, latency targets, avg sequence length, concurrency, current infra (k8s, GPU types).
- Ask about owners for integration (who owns embeddings/inference routing?).
- Quick demo pitch: show Dedicated + Private pattern; describe rollout (canary -> A/B -> fallback).
- Close: propose concrete next step — 2-week POC, Redwood provides test model + infra profile; they provide test dataset or synthetic traffic.

Objection handling (common)
- "We already host inference in-house": Ask cost+ops overhead; offer side-by-side TCO and a small scoped POC to compare. Emphasize we integrate with existing model artifacts and can run in their VPC.
- "Security / PII concerns": Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) + KMS/HSM and audit logs. Offer security checklist and willingness to do architecture review with their SecOps.
- "Vendor lock-in": Explain deployment abstraction and ability to pin model versions; exportable KV/cache; options for on-prem bundle if they insist. Offer contract language for portability.
- "Too expensive": Run numbers with their expected qps and sequence length. Show Optimize suggestions: batching/caching/quantization can dramatically cut unit cost. Offer initial trial credits for pilot.

POC sketch (2-week pilot)
- Week 0: kick-off, access and security review (SSE/IT), decide scope (one model endpoint: merch scoring)
- Week 1: deploy model variant on Redwood Dedicated (or Private if requested), run synthetic traffic + baseline capture from their staging, measure latency/cost + ops runbook handoff
- Week 2: run A/B test on a small % of traffic or offline replay; deliver simple dashboard: latency, cost per 100k requests, error rate, token breakdown
- Deliverable: POC report + proposal for production capacity and pricing options

Open questions / research items (todo)
- Confirm actual qps and concurrent requests for top merchants + peak times (Black Friday-like windows) — ask during first call.
- Which data classification level is the merch scoring data (PII? sensitive?) Need to know for Private requirement.
- Who is the procurement contact and typical lead time for vendor onboarding?
- Get sample model (artifact): architecture (decoder/encoder) and typical seq lengths.

Next steps (concrete)
- Reach out to Head of ML (Marco Liu suggested an intro) — Marco offered to warm intro, follow up in Slack.
- Draft 1-pager POC (for execs) — assign to Sofia to refine with numbers by Fri.
- Prepare security checklist and one-pager on Private deployment + KMS for SecOps.
- Schedule exploratory 30m next week: propose Tue/Thu 11–12 CT.

Notes to self
- Keep outreach short; avoid platform feature dump. Lead with predictable economics + low ops overhead.
- Bring one concrete recent retail case study (numbers) – ask PMM for sanitized metrics.
- Track any signals from earnings call for cost pressure — use as leverage.

End of scratchpad.

(If this proves useful, convert to cleaned one-pager and put on shared drive under shared_drives/company/deals/barnaby.)
